Your job is to inspect the public GitHub repository `https://github.com/canada-ca/content-analysis` and produce a JSON file at `/workspace/manual_content-analysis.json`.

You must determine these exact fields with the exact keys:

1. `bilingual`: Read the README (or at least the first few hundred lines). Does it contain meaningful content in both English and French? Look for French words/phrases, French section headers, or a clear French translation. Allowed: `Yes`/`No`/`Unknown`.
2. `readme_clarity`: Read the README. Does it clearly explain what the project is, who it's for, and how to use it? Allowed: `Poor`/`Fair`/`Good`/`Unknown`.
3. `security_policy`: Check for `SECURITY.md` in root, `.github/`, and `docs/`. If not found, write `Missing`. If found, read it. If it contains real responsible disclosure instructions (contact info, how to report, PGP key, etc.), write `Present`. If it exists but is just a placeholder or links without real instructions, write `Incomplete`. Allowed: `Present`/`Incomplete`/`Missing`/`Unknown`.
4. `issue_response_quality`: Look at the 5 most recently updated open issues (API `https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/content-analysis/issues?state=open&sort=updated&direction=desc`, filter out PRs). For each, check if anyone other than the original reporter commented within the last 6 months (from 2026-07-13). If at least one issue has such a comment, write `Active`. If none, write `Stale`. If there are no open issues, write `No Issues`. Allowed: `Active`/`Stale`/`No Issues`/`Unknown`.
5. `release_notes_quality`: Check the Releases page (API `https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/content-analysis/releases` or HTML). If no releases, write `No Releases`. If releases exist, check the latest few. If the description actually explains what changed (e.g., bullet points, changelog), write `Detailed`. If it's just a version number or tag with no description, write `Version-only`. Allowed: `Detailed`/`Version-only`/`No Releases`/`Unknown`.

- Prefer public HTML page scraping over GitHub API where possible to avoid rate limits. If using API, add `sleep 1` between requests.
- Write the final JSON to `/workspace/manual_content-analysis.json`.

# Consultation Content Analysis (pilot)

[](#consultation-content-analysis-pilot)

OpenNorth’s exploration of preprocessing and content analysis of comments from public consultation datasets using Python. These steps are intended to be applied to data in CSV format from public consultations. Note that responses to questions can only be processed one at a time.

generate --> describe --> preprocessing --> analyze

---

# Analyse du contenu des consultations (pilote)

[](#analyse-du-contenu-des-consultations-pilote)

Exploration, réalisée par NordOuvert en langage Python, du prétraitement et de l’analyse du contenu des commentaires contenus dans les ensembles de données tirées des consultations publiques. Ces étapes doivent être appliquées en format CSV (valeurs séparées par des virgules) aux données des consultations publiques. Veuillez prendre note que les réponses aux questions de recherche ne peuvent être traitées qu’une seule à la fois.

générer --> décrire --> prétraiter --> analyse

---

Preprocessing:

• Manual formatting: Ensure that the input dataset is in CSV format. Each row in the CSV should reflect an independent data entry and each column should be an associated metadata or attribute field. The first row should contain column headers.

• Make note of the CSV columns (starting at 0) that correspond to the ID field, Comment field (only select one response column at a time if the dataset contains multiple), Participant Information field, Event field, and Date field. Refer to instructions in the “generate\_csv” script if any of this information is missing.

• Change necessary variables in the “generate\_csv” script to create a new CSV file that is of appropriate structure

• Change the necessary variables in the “describe\_csv” script to create a new text file with basic descriptions of the dataset
